turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm interviewing people for the spare room in my flat. What should I ask them?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask about their routine, like when they work and when they go to bed. Clashing schedules cause a lot of friction.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, also, My partner and I want to get into longer strategy games for winter, but we've only played easy ones.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you hold your comments till I've gone through every choice? I'll tell you when I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A farming game where you grow crops, raise animals and feed your family, about two hours.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A space exploration game with lots of little cards and combos, quite chunky, maybe three hours.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A two player only card game about building a civilisation through the ages, under an hour.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A detective campaign where you solve cases over a dozen evenings, more story than strategy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Phew, done. Tell me what you think.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Coming from easy games, the two player civilisation one is a great step up, deep but short. The farming game is a classic next step. I'd save the space game until you're hooked, it's a lot.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ask how they feel about guests, cleaning and shared food. And how they handled problems with past flatmates.
